## 1. What was read

**779 research articles** from 32 of the 33 journals on the roster.

A further **129** records (14% of the 908 this month's harvest returned) carry no abstract and are not research: news, correspondence, editor highlights and obituaries. PubMed types them `Journal Article` and nothing else, so the publication-type filter cannot see them — across the whole index they are 22.7% of it and 35% of `general`, and 3,801 of them are JAMA. Every count below is over the full harvest and is inflated by this; the figure above is not.

| General | Cancer | Immune | Bioinfo | Sysbio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 412 | 138 | 81 | 254 | 23 |

!!! warning "Volume swing against the median month: cancer -26%"
    Check the source before reading anything into this. Two benign causes account for most of these. `bioinfo` every January carries the Nucleic Acids Research database issue and runs high. And several journals simply deposit nothing in some months: across the 44 months read, 4 of 33 journals are absent from at least one, worst being *Nat Mach Intell* (20 months missing, 81 papers in total) and *Bioinformatics* (4 months missing, 2,905 papers in total). This month is missing *Nat Mach Intell*. Queried directly, PubMed returns zero for those journal-months too — the holes are in the source, reproduced exactly by re-running the harvest. So a swing here is not evidence that a field went quiet, and is not usually evidence that the pipeline broke either.

Largest contributors: Nature 123, Science 97, Nucleic Acids Res 96, Bioinformatics 53, JAMA 47, Cell 35.

## 3. The evidence that moved it









**Three single-cell foundation-model results in one journal in one month.**
[38409223](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38409223/) (scGPT) and [38844628](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38844628/) (a large-scale single-cell
transcriptomics foundation model) are published in *Nature Methods* in August
2024, and [38528186](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38528186/) is beside them: GPT-4, given marker genes, annotates
cell types across hundreds of tissue and cell types with strong concordance with
manual annotation, shipped as the R package GPTCelltype. Two models built for
single-cell data and one general-purpose model transferring onto a single-cell
task, in one issue. The corpus's November 2025 briefing claimed the virtual-cell
vocabulary had just arrived; the 2025 backfill moved that to spring 2025; the
models are here, in the field's methods journal, in August 2024. The dating is
what fails, repeatedly, not the models.

!!! note "Corrected 2026-08-27"
    This paragraph was headed "— and so does their audit", and closed: "**the
    models and their critics have been in the same journal in the same month
    since the models existed.** There was never a lag to measure." The third
    paper is not an audit. "Assessing" in its title was read as a critique; the
    abstract is an endorsement — "can accurately annotate cell types", "strong
    concordance" — with no adverse finding anywhere in it, and its stance is now
    `supports` with `method-credibility` removed. So this issue of *Nature
    Methods* contains three results and no criticism of any of them, and the
    co-presence claim cannot be made from it. The month's benchmarks are
    elsewhere: the two *Genome Biology* ones in section 4(b), both carded
    `neutral` because neither reports an adverse finding, and the AlphaFold2
    self-estimate benchmark immediately below, which does.

**The audit reaches the model's own confidence.** [39115813](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39115813/): benchmarking
AlphaFold2's accuracy self-estimates against independent model-quality measures.
Not the prediction — the prediction's stated confidence.

## 4. Refutations

### (a) Landing on a tracked thread

[39121849](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39121849/) (*Cell*) is a support rather than a refutation and is filed as
one: blockade of LAG-3 and PD-1 co-expresses cytotoxic and exhaustion modules in
CD8 T cells. It is here because it is the last month in 2024 in which a
next-generation checkpoint appears in a top-tier general journal with a
mechanistic result attached.

### (b) Method credibility

[39152456](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39152456/) and [39123269](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39123269/) (*Genome Biol*) benchmark single-cell
chromatin analysis and spatial transcriptomics clustering, alignment and
integration. Two benchmarks of two modalities in one journal in one month. The
`method-credibility` thread's real content in 2024 is this: the genre is
established, monthly, and concentrated in two journals. What changes later is
volume, and — measured under one consistent rule for the first time on
2026-08-26 — that change happens in 2026, not in 2025 as this corpus recorded.
